p: Here is, 1. The mischief of drunkenness: Wine is a mocker; strong drink is raging. It is so to the sinner himself; it mocks him, makes a fool of him, promises him that satisfaction which it can never give him. …
It is here observed to the honour of a good man, 1. That he does well for himself. …

Note, 1. Those that indulge themselves in their ease may expect to want necessaries, which should have been gotten by honest labour. See here 1. What arts men use to get a good bargain and to buy cheap. …

Two sorts of people are dangerous to be conversed with:—1. Tale-bearers, though they are commonly flatterers, and by fair speeches insinuate themselves into men's acquaintance. Here is, 1. An undutiful child become very wicked by degrees. …

Two things, by which God is greatly affronted, men are here said to be ensnared by, and entangled not only in guilt, but in trouble and ruin at length:—1. Sacrilege, men's alienating holy things and converting them to their own… See here, 1. What is the business of magistrates. …
